newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-SPAIN END CZECH WORLD CUP HOPES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SPAIN END CZECH WORLD CUP HOPES.

text.p: The Czech Republic, beaten European championship finalists last year, were left without any chance of reaching next year's World Cup finals when they lost 1-0 to Spain on Sunday.
Spain took the match with a disputed penalty just before halftime and kept their one-point lead over Yugoslavia at the top of European group six.
With two games left to play, Spain also dramatically increased their chances of qualifying either as group winners or as the best-placed second team in the European groups.
The Spaniards scored in the 40th minute when striker Alfonso Perez slipped through and dived as he rounded Pavel Srnicek.
Although the Czech goalkeeper appeared not to touch Alfonso, the referee had no hesitation in pointing to the spot.

The goal came shortly after Spanish manager Javier Clemente had turned the game around by moving Rafael Alkorta to left back, a position that midfielder Emilio Amavisca had filled in the absence of injured Barcelona defender Sergi Barjuan.
"We were having problems with (Radoslav) Latal," said Clemente. "We had to make a change. It was a risk, we were left a bit exposed in midfield."
Until the change Amavisca had looked out of his depth and the visitors missed a clear chance when Rene Wagner blasted over in the 22nd minute.
Moments later Wagner was unlucky enough to block a fierce shot from team mate Vladimir Smicer.
The Czechs started strongly again after the break but lacked bite in attack as the improvised Spanish defence settled down.
"I know it didn't look very good," said Clemente, who before the game had appealed to fans in Valladolid not to expect too much of their players.
"It was very hard, very difficult...At this stage in the season it's too much...we lacked some spark."
Clemente's team must travel to Slovakia in September before ending their campaign at home to the Faroe Islands.
The Faroes' victory over Malta moved them up to fourth in the group, relegating the Czechs to fifth.
